:::{#thm-evidence-lower-bound-decomposition}
#### The log evidence is the ELBO plus a divergence

Let $p(x, z)$ and $q$ be as in @def-evidence-lower-bound,
and let $p(x) = \sum_z p(x, z)$ be the [evidence](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/bayesian-inference.html#def-marginal-likelihood) of the data,
also called its [marginal likelihood](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/bayesian-inference.html#def-marginal-likelihood).
The evidence is nonzero because the data was observed.
Then the [logarithm](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-logarithm) of the evidence is the [ELBO](#def-evidence-lower-bound) of $q$
plus the [Kullback--Leibler divergence](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-kl-divergence) of $q$ from the [posterior](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/bayesian-inference.html#def-posterior):

$$\log p(x) = \mathrm{ELBO}(q) + \kldivf{q}{p(\cdot \mid x)}.$$

:::

::: proof

Let $z$ be a value with $q(z) > 0$.
Then $p(z \mid x) \ne 0$ and $p(x, z) = p(z \mid x) \, p(x)$.
Apply $\log$ to both sides and rearrange:

$$\log p(x) = \log p(x, z) - \log p(z \mid x).$$

Add and subtract $\log q(z)$ on the right:

$$\log p(x) = \paren{\log p(x, z) - \log q(z)} + \paren{\log q(z) - \log p(z \mid x)}.$$

Multiply both sides by $q(z)$, then sum over the values $z$ with $q(z) > 0$.
The left side sums to $\log p(x)$, because $q$ sums to $1$:

$$\log p(x) = \sum_z q(z) \paren{\log p(x, z) - \log q(z)} + \sum_z q(z) \paren{\log q(z) - \log p(z \mid x)}.$$

The first sum is $\mathrm{ELBO}(q)$ by its definition.
The second sum is $\kldivf{q}{p(\cdot \mid x)}$ by the definition of the divergence.

:::
